title: Rejection of Applications for Vocational Drivers' Licences due to Criminal Record
what_it_is: Rejection of Applications for Vocational Drivers' Licences due to Criminal Record

sections.label: Vocational licence applications rejected criminal records
sections.summary: In 2022, 226 of over 15,000 vocational licence applications were rejected for criminal records, and 72 of 169 appeals were acceded to.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: Of the more than 15,000 vocational licence, or VL, applications across the different services in 2022, 226 applications or about 1.5% were rejected due to criminal records, including murder, rape and kidnapping.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: It is necessary for Land Transport Authority (LTA) to screen the VL applications to safeguard the interests of the commuting public.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: LTA may consider appeals from applicants with criminal records depending on the nature of the case.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: In 2022, 72 out of these 169 appeals were acceded to.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: LTA considers such appeals carefully to strike a balance between allowing applicants who committed less severe offences to take on driving as a vocation while safeguarding the safety of passengers.

sections.label: Appeals assessed case by case
sections.summary: Appeals for offences beyond murder, rape and kidnapping are considered case by case, based on severity, timing and mitigating factors.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: Besides murder, rape and kidnapping, there is a real wide range of such offences.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: We will consider them on a case-by-case basis because it is not just the severity of the offence, but also when the offence was committed, and also any other mitigating factors like recalcitrance and so on.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: So, when an appeal comes in, we will look at it on a case-by-case basis, based on its own merit and make an independent assessment.
